items.title: Drivers warn against repeating Saturday's conditions in the Race
items.summary: George Russell warned that repeating Saturday's opening wet conditions in the Race could create a high risk of a serious incident; Carlos Sainz described the first laps as sketchy, and Isack Hadjar said the full wets lacked grip. These are drivers' assessments after Qualifying, not a Race Control decision or a current forecast. Pirelli's 7 November report cited a 60% race-day rain chance when it was published.
items.why_it_matters: Cars must follow more closely in a race than in qualifying, changing the visibility and aquaplaning risks. Keep Pirelli's dated rain probability separate from the live forecast and any decision to run.

items.title: Norris takes pole; official grid confirms penalty-adjusted order
items.summary: Formula1.com's official 22-car Qualifying result and FIA Document 50's final classification agree: Lando Norris took pole in 1:27.470, 0.204s ahead of George Russell, with Kimi Antonelli third. The official Starting Grid now lists all 22 entrants after penalties, including Russell seventh, Leclerc 14th, Hamilton 20th, Verstappen 21st and Perez 22nd.
items.why_it_matters: Keep the FIA/Formula1.com qualifying classification distinct from the penalty-adjusted official grid. The Race's earlier post-penalty order was provisional and is no longer needed to fill an unavailable-results gap.

items.title: Hamilton's cumulative 75-place penalty; Verstappen targets a fun recovery
items.summary: FIA Documents 42–43 add 65 places to Hamilton's earlier 10-place drop; he qualified 11th and the official Starting Grid lists him 20th. Verstappen's FIA Document 33 imposes a 30-place drop, and the 22-car official grid lists him 21st.
items.why_it_matters: Keep the component sanctions and qualifying classification distinct from the penalty-adjusted official grid; the grid, rather than the earlier provisional order, confirms Hamilton and Verstappen's starting positions.

items.title: Pirelli prefers a dry two-stop; published set chart omits used quantities
items.summary: Using Friday FP2 as the only representative long-run data, Pirelli estimates a Soft–Medium–Soft two-stop about three seconds quicker than using all three slick compounds, while a one-stop is around ten seconds slower. Coffee Corner Motorsport's separate Pirelli-credited chart shows S–M–S laps 17–23/42–48, M–H–S 23–29/50–56, S–H–S 16–22/44–50 and M–H 28–34; those are chart scenarios, not Pirelli-published lap windows. Its 22-row image shows four new Softs for the ten Q3 entrants, five for the others, and one new Medium and Hard per driver. The graphic omits used-set cells, so no complete six-cell inventory is transcribed.
items.why_it_matters: These are simulated dry-race options, not measured outcomes; wet conditions could displace them. The full credited image remains available, but missing used-set quantities must not be inferred.

items.title: Perez warned; Bearman reprimanded in separate steward decisions
items.summary: FIA Document 40 resolves Perez's FP3 summons: after reviewing video, the Stewards found he threw a small plastic cable organiser that had detached from his seat belt; Cadillac received a formal warning. Separately, Document 41 reprimands Bearman for reversing under his own power in the pit lane during Qualifying; it is his second reprimand of the season.
items.why_it_matters: Neither decision changes the official starting grid. Keep Perez's warning and Bearman's reprimand distinct from Perez's 30-place power-unit sanction.
